case_title: N Parameswaran Unni v. G Kannan and Another
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act s.138 rlw. s.142
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to simple imprisonment of three months
offence_finally_established: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
neutral_facts: The accused borrowed a total of Rs. 64,000 from the complainant and issued three cheques, two of which were returned by the bank as dishonoured. The complainant received an intimation from the bank about the dishonour of the cheques on 08.04.1991. The complainant issued a legal notice to the accused on 12.04.1991, which was returned with a postal endorsement indicating the addressee was absent. The complainant sent another legal notice on 04.05.1991, which was returned with a postal endorsement indicating it was refused. The complainant then filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The Trial Court convicted the accused, and the Appellate Court upheld the conviction. The High Court reversed the conviction, arguing that the second notice was sent beyond the 15-day limit. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, finding that the first notice was valid and the second notice was merely a reminder.
